_about: How AmPanel's exit guard ends each emulator when the exit key (Esc) is pressed during a game. Rules match the game's process name (exe) or its window class. close: 'self' = the emulator closes on Esc by itself (just wait), 'altf4' = send Alt+F4 to its window, 'close' = WM_CLOSE to its windows, 'kill' = end it at once. grace = ms to wait first (gives 'self' emulators time). Anything not listed: wait 1500 ms, WM_CLOSE, then end the process tree after 3 s. First rules came from James's CabinetLauncher AutoHotkey script. A cabinet's own <manifest>\exit-rules.json is read first and wins.

rules._why: C64: Esc is RUN/STOP in VICE - hold Esc to end
PC games use Esc for their own menus
RACE / DRIVE builds name the PC launcher PC Games: PC games use Esc for their own menus (GRID, Batman) - hold Esc to end
RetroBat's RetroArch does not quit on Esc; LEGENDS' may - 1 s covers both
Model 2 emulator (Daytona USA): Esc only drops it out of full screen into a window, it never quits on its own - close it at once (RACE1 2026-11-28)
American Truck Simulator (Steam) runs outside the launched chain and ignores WM_CLOSE (RACE1 2026-11-27: holding Esc did not end it); Alt+F4 quits
Euro Truck Simulator 2: same engine as American Truck Simulator
